usage: Most common verb pairing; the ceremony is an event you attend
Set phrase for the couple holding/having their wedding; sounds more natural than 결혼식을 하다
Add -장 for the physical venue; also called 예식장
You receive a 청첩장 (invitation) for this
examples: 다음 주 토요일에 친구 결혼식이 있어서 못 가요.
I can't go because I have a friend's wedding next Saturday.
Weekend weddings are the norm in Korea, so this is a very common excuse
결혼식은 보통 30분에서 1시간이면 끝나요.
Weddings usually end in 30 minutes to an hour.
Korean weddings are short; the meal afterward matters more socially
결혼식 끝나고 식당에서 밥 먹고 가세요.
After the wedding, please eat at the dining hall before you leave.
The buffet/meal after is expected; your 축의금 covers it
nuance: 결혼식 is the ceremony itself, while 결혼 is the marriage/getting married. In Korea the ceremony is often surprisingly brief and the real social event is the meal afterward, which your cash gift (축의금) pays toward. Saying 결혼식에 가요 signals you're attending as a guest.
mistakes: Don't confuse 결혼식 (the ceremony) with 결혼 (marriage); '결혼했어요' means you got married, not that you attended a wedding.
Avoid 결혼식을 가다; the natural particle is 에 — 결혼식에 가다.

usage: Standard verb; you attend to pay respects
Often inside or attached to a hospital; where the wake is held
More formal than 가다; common in workplace contexts
Said of the bereaved family holding the funeral (drop -식)
examples: 부장님 아버님 장례식에 다 같이 갔어요.
We all went together to our manager's father's funeral.
Attending a coworker's family funeral is a strong workplace obligation in Korea
장례식장에서는 보통 검은 옷을 입어요.
People usually wear black clothes at the funeral hall.
Dark, plain clothing is expected; bright colors are inappropriate
장례식에 가서 조의금을 냈어요.
I went to the funeral and gave a condolence gift.
Cash in a white envelope (조의금) is the customary gesture
nuance: Korean funerals (장례식) typically run three days and are held at a 장례식장, frequently located within a hospital. Attending the wake of a colleague's or friend's family member is a significant social duty, and you bring 조의금 in a plain white envelope. Wear muted, dark clothing.
mistakes: Don't bring or say 축하 (congratulations) anything; the correct sentiment is 삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다 or simply offering condolences.
Don't confuse the white-envelope 조의금 (funeral) with the wedding 축의금; mixing them up is a serious faux pas.

usage: Said of the parents throwing the party
You may get invited by coworkers or friends with a baby
Small gift the parents give guests in thanks (떡, towels, etc.)
The highlight where the baby picks an object predicting its future
examples: 동료 아기 돌잔치에 초대받아서 갔어요.
I was invited to my coworker's baby's first-birthday party, so I went.
A common reason to give a baby gift or cash
돌잔치에서 아기가 돌잡이로 마이크를 잡았어요.
At the doljanchi the baby grabbed the microphone in the doljabi.
Guests cheer for whichever object the baby picks
요즘은 돌잔치를 작게 가족끼리만 하기도 해요.
These days some people hold the doljanchi small, just with family.
Lavish hall parties are declining; intimate ones are trendy now
nuance: 돌 is a baby's first birthday, historically a milestone because infant mortality was high, and 돌잔치 is the celebration. The signature moment is 돌잡이, where the baby grabs an object said to foretell its future. As a guest you typically give cash or a gift, and lavish hall-style parties have become more low-key recently.
mistakes: 돌잔치 is specifically the FIRST birthday; don't use it for ordinary birthdays — that's just 생일.
Note the spelling 돌잔치 (one word), not 돌 잔치 with a space.

usage: 맞다 = to greet/reach a milestone date
Family often gives a trip or money rather than a big party now
Use honorific 이세요 since it's about an elder
examples: 올해 아버지가 환갑이셔서 가족 여행을 가요.
My father turns 60 this year, so we're taking a family trip.
Trips have largely replaced big banquets for hwangap
예전에는 환갑잔치를 크게 했어요.
In the past people held big 60th-birthday banquets.
When life expectancy was shorter, reaching 60 was a major event
할머니 환갑 때 가족이 다 모였어요.
The whole family gathered for grandmother's 60th birthday.
환갑 is a key family milestone that brings relatives together
nuance: 환갑 (also written 회갑) marks turning 60, the completion of the traditional 60-year zodiac cycle, once a rare and celebrated age. Today, with longer lifespans, the big 환갑잔치 banquet has faded and families more often mark it with a trip or gift. Always refer to an elder's 환갑 with honorifics.
mistakes: Because it concerns an elder, use honorific forms: 환갑이세요, not the plain 환갑이에요.
환갑 is the 60th by Korean age counting tied to the zodiac cycle; don't assume it maps exactly onto a Western 'turning 60' in every context.

usage: The couple hands or sends it to you
Implies you're expected to attend or send 축의금
Sent via KakaoTalk link; now extremely common
Casual phrase for handing them around to friends and coworkers
examples: 어제 친구한테 모바일 청첩장 받았어요.
I got a mobile wedding invitation from my friend yesterday.
KakaoTalk links have largely replaced paper invitations
청첩장 주려고 일부러 만났어요.
We met up on purpose so they could give me the invitation.
Handing a paper 청첩장 in person is a courteous gesture
청첩장에 식장 위치랑 시간이 다 적혀 있어요.
The venue location and time are all written on the invitation.
Mobile ones include a map link and account number for 축의금
nuance: 청첩장 is the wedding invitation, increasingly sent as a 모바일 청첩장 (KakaoTalk link) rather than printed paper. Receiving one signals you're expected either to attend or to send 축의금. The mobile version usually bundles a map, schedule, and the couple's bank account number for transferring the cash gift.
mistakes: Don't confuse 청첩장 (wedding invitation) with 초대장 (a general invitation card); 청첩장 is specifically for weddings.
Getting a 청첩장 carries a soft obligation — ignoring it from a close friend or coworker can strain the relationship.

usage: 내다 is the standard verb at the reception desk
Used when you can't attend and transfer it instead
White envelope you write your name on at the desk
A common baseline amount; closer relationships give more
examples: 결혼식에 못 가서 축의금만 계좌로 보냈어요.
I couldn't make the wedding, so I just sent the cash gift to their account.
Sending it by bank transfer is fully acceptable if you can't attend
축의금은 보통 5만 원이나 10만 원 내요.
People usually give 50,000 or 100,000 won.
Amount depends on closeness; odd-numbered bills are traditional
접수처에서 축의금 봉투에 이름 적어서 냈어요.
I wrote my name on the envelope and handed it in at the reception desk.
You sign the envelope so the couple knows who gave it
nuance: 축의금 is the cash you give at a wedding, placed in a white envelope and handed in at the 접수처 (reception desk), where you sign so the couple can record it. Amounts run roughly 50,000 won and up depending on closeness, traditionally in odd denominations. If you can't attend, transferring it to their account is perfectly normal.
mistakes: Don't mix up 축의금 (weddings/happy events) with 조의금 (funerals); using the wrong word or envelope is a real social error.
Avoid even-numbered amounts like 60,000 or 80,000; odd amounts (50,000 / 70,000 / 100,000) are customary.

usage: 내다 at the funeral reception desk
부의금 and 조의금 are used interchangeably
examples: 회사 동료 부모님 장례식에 조의금을 냈어요.
I gave condolence money at my coworker's parent's funeral.
A standard workplace courtesy in Korea
조의금 봉투에는 보통 부의라고 써요.
On the condolence envelope you usually write 부의.
부의 or 조의 is written on the front, unlike a wedding envelope
멀어서 못 가고 조의금만 동료 편에 보냈어요.
I couldn't go because it was far, so I sent the condolence money with a coworker.
Sending it with someone attending is common when you can't go
nuance: 조의금 (also 부의금) is the cash given to a bereaved family, placed in a plain white envelope, often with 부의 written on the front. It's offered at the 장례식장 reception desk and, like 축의금, is a near-obligatory gesture for coworkers' family funerals. The envelope and occasion are solemn, so keep everything understated.
mistakes: Never reuse a colorful or wedding-style envelope; 조의금 requires a plain white one.
Don't confuse 조의금 (funerals) with 축의금 (weddings); the contexts are opposite and the mistake is serious.

usage: Add -지 for the place; e.g. 하와이, 몰디브
go and come back from a honeymoon
다녀오다 = the round trip is done
신혼 alone refers to the early-married phase; 신혼집 = newlywed home
examples: 결혼식 끝나고 바로 신혼여행을 떠났어요.
Right after the wedding they left for their honeymoon.
Couples often fly out the same day or next day
신혼여행은 발리로 갔다 왔어요.
We went to Bali for our honeymoon.
Southeast Asian beach resorts are popular choices
신혼여행 다녀와서 집들이를 했어요.
After the honeymoon we held a housewarming.
Ties naturally to 집들이, another life-event word
nuance: 신혼여행 is the honeymoon, literally the 'newlywed trip,' usually taken right after the 결혼식. Beach resorts in Southeast Asia and longer-haul spots like Hawaii or Europe are typical 신혼여행지. The root 신혼 covers the broader newlywed period, as in 신혼집 (the couple's first home).
mistakes: Don't shorten it to just 여행 when you mean the honeymoon specifically; 여행 is any trip.
신혼여행 is one word — avoid writing 신혼 여행 with a space.

usage: 반지 = ring; the ring exchanged at engagement
Antonym verb worth knowing (파혼 = broken engagement)
examples: 저희 언니가 지난달에 약혼했어요.
My older sister got engaged last month.
약혼하다 is the natural way to announce it
약혼자랑 같이 상견례를 준비하고 있어요.
I'm preparing the family meeting with my fiancé.
Links to 상견례, the families' introductory meal
요즘은 약혼식을 따로 안 하는 사람도 많아요.
These days many people don't hold a separate engagement ceremony.
Formal engagement ceremonies are less common now
nuance: 약혼 is the formal engagement, with the verb 약혼하다 and your partner called 약혼자. In modern Korea a separate 약혼식 (engagement ceremony) is increasingly skipped; couples often move straight from agreeing to marry into the 상견례 and wedding prep. The opposite, calling it off, is 파혼.
mistakes: Don't confuse 약혼 (engagement) with 결혼 (marriage); 약혼한 사이 means engaged, not married.
약혼자 covers both fiancé and fiancée — there's no separate gendered word to memorize.

english: formal meeting of the two families (before marriage)
usage: Said of the two families meeting
The people 상견례 brings together (양가 = both houses)
examples: 다음 주에 양가 부모님 상견례가 있어요.
Next week the parents of both families are meeting.
A major step toward the wedding
상견례는 조용한 한정식집에서 했어요.
We held the family meeting at a quiet Korean-set-menu restaurant.
Calm, upscale restaurants are typical venues
상견례 때 너무 긴장돼서 말을 별로 못 했어요.
I was so nervous at the family meeting I could barely talk.
It's a formal, slightly tense occasion
nuance: 상견례 is the formal first meeting between the two families before a wedding, where both sets of parents (양가 부모님) are introduced over a meal. It's a significant, somewhat formal milestone usually held at a quiet, refined restaurant, and going smoothly signals the families approve of the union.
mistakes: 상견례 specifically means the two families meeting before marriage — don't use it for any general first meeting between people.
It's a formal occasion, so dress and speak politely; treating it casually can offend the in-laws-to-be.

usage: Said of the host throwing the party
Detergent or toilet paper are classic choices
Host inviting friends to the new place
examples: 이사하고 나서 친구들 불러서 집들이를 했어요.
After moving I invited friends over for a housewarming.
집들이 usually follows soon after 이사 (moving)
집들이 갈 때 보통 휴지나 세제를 사 가요.
When going to a housewarming people usually bring toilet paper or detergent.
These gifts symbolize wishes for the household's prosperity
주말에 새집 집들이에 초대받았어요.
I was invited to a housewarming at their new place this weekend.
A common, relaxed social gathering among friends
nuance: 집들이 is the housewarming party thrown after moving into a new home (이사). The classic gifts are toilet paper (휴지) and laundry detergent (세제): the paper symbolizes things unrolling smoothly, the detergent's bubbles symbolize prosperity bubbling up. It's a warm, casual event where the host usually cooks or orders in for friends.
mistakes: Bringing 휴지 or 세제 is a kind, traditional gesture, not a cheap one — don't assume it's an odd gift.
집들이 is the party; don't confuse it with 이사 (the act of moving) — you do 이사 first, then 집들이.

usage: Often arrives via KakaoTalk or workplace message
The text giving the deceased's name, 빈소, and funeral times
examples: 오늘 아침에 부장님 어머님 부고를 받았어요.
This morning I received notice of our manager's mother's passing.
Workplace 부고 messages circulate quickly and call for attendance
부고 문자에 장례식장 위치가 적혀 있었어요.
The death-notice text had the funeral hall's location written on it.
The message bundles 빈소 location and visiting hours
부고를 듣고 바로 조의금을 준비했어요.
On hearing of the death I prepared condolence money right away.
Receiving a 부고 prompts 조의금 and a visit if you're close
nuance: 부고 is the formal notification that someone has died, typically circulated by family or coworkers as a 부고 문자 listing the deceased, the 빈소 (wake location), and visiting times. In a workplace, receiving a colleague's family 부고 effectively signals that attending the funeral and giving 조의금 is expected. The word and tone are solemn.
mistakes: 부고 is the death NOTICE, not the funeral itself (that's 장례식); you receive a 부고 and then attend the 장례식.
Respond to a 부고 soberly — no emoji or light replies in the KakaoTalk thread; a simple condolence message is right.
